title: TRAI DND Regulations 2018
body: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India DND regulations: Commercial communications (promotional messages) are prohibited to DND-registered numbers. However, transactional messages related to existing business relationships are exempt from DND restrictions. Service messages, OTPs, and payment confirmations are classified as transactional. Recovery messages for genuine failed transactions fall under transactional exemption when sent within 30 days of the original transaction. If DND blocks SMS/voice, switch channel to WhatsApp or email.

title: Communication Time Restrictions
body: As per TRAI guidelines, commercial and transactional communications via SMS and voice calls should be restricted to the window of 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM IST. Messages sent outside this window may be flagged by telecom operators and could result in sender ID blocking. WhatsApp and email communications are not directly regulated by TRAI time windows but best practice recommends respecting the same window. If outside window, schedule delivery for 9 AM next day.

title: Failed Transaction Refund Timeline
body: RBI mandates that failed transaction amounts must be auto-reversed within T+5 business days. If the amount is not reversed, the acquiring bank is liable to pay compensation at the rate of ₹100 per day of delay. Merchants should not attempt to recover payments that have already been auto-reversed by the bank. Recovery notifications must clearly state that the customer is being asked to re-initiate payment, not that money is being debited from them.

title: Information Technology Act - Consent Requirements
body: Under the Information Technology Act 2000 and subsequent amendments, explicit consent is required for sending electronic communications for payment recovery. The first communication must include an opt-out mechanism. Once a customer opts out, all further recovery communications must cease immediately. Violations can attract penalties under Section 66A. Recovery payment links must be served over HTTPS with valid SSL certificates.

title: Recovery Communication Standards
body: All recovery communications must: 1) Clearly identify the merchant/sender, 2) Include the exact amount due and original order reference, 3) Provide a dispute resolution mechanism or support link, 4) Not use threatening, coercive, or deceptive language, 5) Maintain customer dignity and respect. AI-generated recovery messages must follow the same tone standards as human-drafted messages. Payment links must show the correct amount and merchant name.

title: Consumer Protection Act 2019
body: Under the Consumer Protection Act 2019: 1) Recovery messages must not constitute unfair trade practice, 2) Customer has the right to be informed about the reason for payment failure, 3) Customer has the right to opt out of further communications, 4) Excessive or harassing recovery attempts can be reported to the Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. Since recovery only sends payment links (not auto-debits), the customer retains full control over whether to complete payment.

title: Message Frequency Cap
body: Industry best practice recommends a maximum of 5 recovery messages per day per customer across all channels combined. Exceeding this limit increases the risk of: 1) Customer complaint to TRAI/RBI, 2) WhatsApp number being flagged for spam, 3) Email domain reputation damage, 4) Customer churn. Recovery messages should be spaced at least 4 hours apart. Multi-channel recovery flows (e.g. WhatsApp then SMS fallback) count as separate messages toward this cap.

title: High-Value Transaction Advisory
body: For transactions exceeding ₹10,000, recovery notifications should include additional context to build customer confidence: 1) Display the full order details and merchant identity, 2) Include a direct merchant support contact, 3) Use the customer's preferred channel, 4) Tag the transaction as high-value in analytics for monitoring. Since recovery only sends payment links (customer must authorize payment themselves), there is no financial risk in sending notifications for any amount.

title: Payment Link Security Standards
body: All recovery payment links must: 1) Be served over HTTPS with valid SSL certificates, 2) Display the correct amount, merchant name, and order reference, 3) Expire within 24 hours of generation to prevent stale link abuse, 4) Support multiple payment methods (UPI, Card, Netbanking) for customer flexibility, 5) Include a Razorpay-verified merchant badge. Links must never auto-debit or pre-authorize — the customer must explicitly complete payment.

title: Channel Escalation Protocol
body: Recovery notifications should follow a progressive escalation strategy: 1) Start with the customer's preferred channel (WhatsApp preferred for highest open rates), 2) If no response within 24 hours, escalate to the next channel (WhatsApp → SMS → Email), 3) Voice calls should only be used for high-value transactions (>₹5,000) or after 2+ failed notification attempts, 4) Never send the same message content on multiple channels simultaneously — space by at least 4 hours, 5) Each escalation step counts toward the daily frequency cap.

title: Recovery Retry Limits
body: Notification retries (re-sending recovery messages) are capped at 3 attempts per transaction. Auto-retries (generating a fresh payment link for the same transaction) are capped at 5 attempts. Each notification retry must be separated by at least 4 hours (cool-off period). After all retries are exhausted, the transaction should be marked as exception and escalated to manual review. Retries should not be attempted during active disputes or chargebacks.

title: Dispute and Chargeback Block
body: When a customer has an active dispute or chargeback: 1) All recovery communications must cease immediately, 2) No payment links should be generated for the disputed transaction, 3) The transaction must be flagged as exception with reason 'active_dispute', 4) Recovery can only resume after the dispute is resolved in the merchant's favor. Sending recovery messages during a dispute may constitute harassment and violate RBI Ombudsman Scheme 2021.
